title: CodemagicPatch anonymous telemetry ingest report (v1)
description: Wire contract for the report body a CodemagicPatch server instance POSTs to the central telemetry ingest endpoint when anonymous usage telemetry is enabled. The body is JSON, normally gzip-compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip), at most 256 KiB after decompression, and carries only aggregated counters — never device identifiers, app/team/deployment identifiers, or URLs. The root schema is the lenient envelope the ingest enforces at runtime; `strictEnvelope` is the exact shape current senders produce and is what sender/ingest contract tests validate fixtures against. See TELEMETRY.md in the codemagic-patch repository for the full protocol description, response semantics, and privacy statement.
$comment: Evolution rules: additive-only within v1. The ingest ignores unknown envelope/instance/record fields, ignores records with an unknown `type` or `event` (the request still succeeds), and coerces unknown `platform` to 'unknown' and unknown `reason` to 'other'. Records whose `type` IS known must satisfy that type's structural definition or the whole request is rejected with 400. `schema_version` is bumped only for breaking changes; v1 remains accepted for at least 24 months after v2 ships.

schema_version.description: Wire-format major version. Always 1 for this schema.

instance_id.description: Random UUID minted once per installation. Anonymous instance identity used for deduplication and instance counting; carries no information about the operator.

report_id.description: UUID minted per built batch. Lets the ingest fast-path exact replays; a batch rebuilt after retry/restart may legitimately carry a NEW report_id, so correctness never depends on this value.

sent_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the sender built the request. Used only for clock-skew monitoring.

instance.description: Coarse, non-identifying instance properties for version-adoption statistics.

records.description: Heterogeneous array of tagged records. Each element declares its shape via the `type` discriminator. Elements with an unknown `type` are ignored individually; elements with a known `type` must satisfy that type's structural definition.

counterRecord.title: Hourly aggregate event counter cell (structural / runtime contract)
counterRecord.description: One count for one (closed UTC hour, event, platform[, reason]) cell, bucketed by the instance's server receive time. Value fields `event`, `platform`, and `reason` are structurally plain bounded strings so that future values remain additive; the ingest ignores records with an unknown `event` and coerces unknown `platform`/`reason`. The strict definitions below pin today's closed value sets.

window_start.description: Inclusive start of the closed UTC hour window (hour-aligned).

window_end.description: Exclusive end of the window; always window_start + 1 hour.

count.description: Number of events in the cell. Positive safe integer; zero cells are never sent. No business ceiling — this is a type/storage constraint only.

dauRecord.title: Daily active devices count (structural / runtime contract)
dauRecord.description: COUNT(DISTINCT device) computed on the instance for one UTC day; only the integer leaves the instance. Re-sent as the day grows; the ingest keeps the greatest value seen.

heartbeatRecord.title: Instance liveness heartbeat (structural / runtime contract)
heartbeatRecord.description: Liveness signal so idle instances still register as alive. Senders include exactly one per request (enforced by strictEnvelope; the ingest tolerates any number).

strictCounterRecord.title: Counter cell exactly as current senders produce it (test contract)

strictDauRecord.title: DAU record exactly as current senders produce it (test contract)

strictHeartbeatRecord.title: Heartbeat record exactly as current senders produce it (test contract)

strictRecord.title: Closed tagged union of the three v1 record shapes (test contract)
strictRecord.description: Used by sender and ingest contract tests to assert fixtures carry only shapes and values current senders are allowed to produce. The runtime ingest deliberately does NOT use this union: an unknown record type must be ignored, not fail the batch.

strictEnvelope.title: Envelope exactly as current senders produce it (test contract)
